name: bKash
tagline: Mobile financial service in Bangladesh for sending money, cash in and out through agents, bill pay and merchant payments.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. The app itself is free to install, revenue comes from cash out and send money fees.

verdictSummary: An AI agent can absolutely build the app you see: a balance, a contact list, a send screen, a transaction history. What it cannot build is the thing that makes the number on the screen mean anything, which is a central bank licence, a trust account holding real taka, KYC on tens of millions of accounts, and a few hundred thousand agents who will hand you physical cash in a market town. bKash is not a payments UI, it is a settlement network wearing a payments UI. Every merchant, utility biller and relative who already has an account is part of the moat, and none of that transfers to your localhost build. The only honest personal version is a ledger that tracks money you moved some other way.
coreLoopDIY: A local ledger app where you log transfers, cash in and cash out by hand against contacts and see running balances, with no actual money moving anywhere.
requirements: Node and a browser, or a phone with a browser
SQLite file or local storage for the ledger
Manual entry of every transaction, because there is no bank feed to pull from
whatYouLose: Actual money movement: your build stores numbers, not funds
The agent network, which is the only reason cash in and cash out work at all
Merchant and utility acceptance, so no bill pay, no shop QR, no salary disbursement
Regulatory standing: holding other people's money without a licence is a crime, not a feature
Fraud handling, PIN security, dispute resolution and the phone support line people actually call
moatNotes: Mobile money is a licensing business with an app attached. The agent network is closer to physical infrastructure than software.
whyPeopleStillPay: People pay the cash out fee because the alternative is a bus ride to a bank branch that closes at four. The value is that the person on the other end already has bKash, the shop on the corner already has bKash, and the electricity board already accepts bKash. That coverage took a decade, a telecom partnership and a central bank licence to assemble. No amount of clean code produces a stranger in another district who will hand your mother cash.
notes: The screens are a one-sitting build; the float, the licence and the agents are not. The moat is regulated custody of real money plus a few hundred thousand humans who dispense cash.
prompt:
Build a local, offline personal money ledger called "Khata" for tracking informal transfers between people. This is a bookkeeping tool only. It never moves real money and must never pretend to.

Stack, no alternatives:
- Vite + React + TypeScript
- SQLite via better-sqlite3 behind a tiny Express API, single process, `npm run dev` starts both
- Plain CSS, no UI framework
- Everything stored in ./data/khata.db, no cloud, no accounts, no telemetry

Data model:
- contacts: id, name, phone (optional), notes
- entries: id, contact_id, direction ('sent' | 'received'), amount (integer minor units), fee (integer, default 0), method ('cash' | 'wallet' | 'bank' | 'other'), occurred_on (date), memo
- All amounts in Bangladeshi taka, formatted with the BDT symbol and thousands separators

Screens:
1. Home: total sent, total received, net position, total fees paid this month, plus the five most recent entries.
2. Contacts list with per-contact net balance, tap through to a per-contact statement.
3. Add entry form: contact (with create-new inline), direction, amount, fee, method, date defaulting to today, memo. Keyboard-first, submits with Enter.
4. History with filters by contact, direction, method and month.

Requirements:
- CSV import and export of entries so data is never trapped.
- A mobile-width layout that works on a phone browser; this will mostly be used on a phone.
- Fees are tracked separately from amounts so the monthly "what did moving money cost me" number is honest.
- Seed the database with about twenty realistic sample entries across five contacts on first run.

Explicitly out of scope, do not build:
- Any payment integration, card processing, bank API or wallet API
- User accounts, auth, multi-tenant anything, PIN screens that imply security you do not have
- Push notifications, KYC flows, agent features

Put a single visible line in the app footer: "Ledger only. No money is moved by this app." Write a README with setup steps and a one-paragraph statement that this is a record keeping tool and not a financial service.
